description: Formula registry for calculating import duties, taxes, fees, and configured export taxes

vat_standard_rate.description: Standard VAT rate per Law on Taxation 2023
vat_standard_rate.applies_to: CIF + Import Duty + Special Tax + Excise Tax

step_1.name: Currency Conversion
step_1.description: Convert CIF to KHR if needed

step_2.name: Rate Lookup
step_2.description: Determine applicable duty rate based on HS code

step_6.name: Total Duties and Taxes
step_6.description: Sum all duties and taxes (round UP)

step_7.name: Fees Calculation
step_7.description: Calculate processing and inspection fees if applicable

step_8.name: Final Total
step_8.description: Sum duties, taxes, and fees (round UP to final amount)

currency_conversion.formula: customs_value_khr = cif_value * exchange_rate (if currency is USD)
currency_conversion.description: Convert CIF value from external currency to KHR using official MEF rate
critical_notes: MUST execute FIRST before any tax calculations
Use official MEF exchange rates - lookup by currency code and date
Use exchange rate EXACTLY as published - DO NOT round it
Round conversion result to whole number only

rate_determination.description: Determine which duty rate to apply

decision_logic.then: Look up hs_code in duty_rates.csv and extract duty_rate from column 4

lookup_details.also_available: Column 5 = special_tax_rate, Column 6 = vat_rate, Column 3 = unit_of_measure

rate_determination.notes: FTA preferential rates not implemented yet - use manual_rates if special agreement applies

cop_amount.description: Calculate COP (Import Taxes) based on customs value and import tax rate

inputs.name: customs_value_khr
inputs.description: Customs value in KHR (converted if needed)

inputs.name: duty_rate
inputs.description: Duty rate from lookup (percentage expressed as decimal)

cop_amount.notes: Varies by HS code and preferential agreements. Always check for exemptions.

sop_amount.description: Calculate SOP (Special Tariff / Special Tax) for specific product categories (Cambodia terminology)

inputs.name: cop_amount
inputs.description: COP amount (already rounded) from previous calculation step

inputs.name: special_tax_rate
inputs.description: Rate specific to product category from duty_rates.csv

vop_amount.formula: vop_amount = vop_base * vat_rate (where vop_base depends on if taxable or non-taxable goods)
vop_amount.description: Calculate VOP (Value Added Tax per Cambodia customs) based on conditional base (taxable vs non-taxable goods)

inputs.name: vop_base
inputs.description: VOP base determined by goods category: (CIF+COP) for non-taxable; (CIF+COP+SOP) for taxable

inputs.name: vat_rate
inputs.description: Standard VAT rate = 10% (per Law on Taxation 2023)

critical_notes: VOP base is conditional: determined in step 4 of rounding_rules.json execution_order
For non-taxable goods (SOP=0): VOP_base = CIF + COP
For general taxable goods (SOP>0): VOP_base = CIF + COP + SOP
Always apply this rule AFTER determining goods category and calculating SOP

total_duties_and_taxes.description: Sum all duty and tax components (COP + SOP + VOP; excludes fees)
total_duties_and_taxes.notes: Rounded UP to nearest 100. This is intermediate, not final payment amount.

total_payable.description: Final amount payable including all duties, taxes, and fees
critical_notes: This is the final payment amount shown on payment receipt
ALWAYS round UP to nearest 100 (no exceptions)

duty_exemption.description: Apply zero duty when valid exemption exists
duty_exemption.notes: Exemptions require proper documentation per applicable sub-decrees

excise_tax.formula: excise_tax = customs_value_khr * excise_rate OR quantity * specific_rate
excise_tax.description: Calculate excise tax (ad-valorem or specific) - NOTE: In Cambodia, excise is typically included in SOP or separate duty

variations.applies_to: Certain petroleum products, beverages by volume

processing_fee.description: Fixed processing fee for customs declaration
processing_fee.notes: Check current fee schedule for applicable amounts

inspection_fee.description: Fee for customs scanning or physical inspection

acfta_duty.description: ACFTA (ASEAN-China Free Trade Area) duty = 0% with Form E

atiga_duty.description: ATIGA agreement duty = 0% with Form D for ASEAN countries

ajcep_duty.description: AJCEP (ASEAN-Japan CEPA) typically reduced or 0% duty

duty_exemption_detailed.notes: Exemptions require proper documentation and authorization per applicable sub-decrees

dv_declared_value.description: DV (Declared Value) - Fair amount of price used to keep the market in the middle, not too high or too low
dv_declared_value.notes: DV is used as the customs valuation basis. Only applies to imports, not exports.

acfta_duty.description: ACFTA (ASEAN-China Free Trade Area) makes customs duty rate 0.00
acfta_duty.notes: ACFTA agreement sets duty to 0% for eligible goods with proper documentation (Form E)

atiga_duty.description: ATIGA (ASEAN Trade in Goods Agreement) makes customs duty rate 0.00 for intra-ASEAN trade
atiga_duty.notes: ATIGA is the most commonly used FTA in Cambodia for trade with ASEAN members. Requires Form D Certificate of Origin.

akfta_duty.description: AKFTA (ASEAN-Korea Free Trade Agreement) duty calculation - rate typically 0% or reduced
akfta_duty.notes: AKFTA provides preferential rates for Korean goods imported to Cambodia. Most goods have 0% duty with Form AK.

ajcep_duty.description: AJCEP (ASEAN-Japan Comprehensive Economic Partnership) duty calculation - rate typically 0% or reduced
ajcep_duty.notes: AJCEP provides preferential rates for Japanese goods imported to Cambodia. Most goods have 0% or reduced duty with Form AJ.

rcep_duty.description: RCEP (Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership) duty calculation - rate varies by origin and commodity
rcep_duty.notes: RCEP is the newest and largest FTA covering 15 countries. Tariff elimination schedules vary by country pair and commodity. Entered into force 2022.

aanzfta_duty.description: AANZFTA (ASEAN-Australia-New Zealand Free Trade Agreement) duty calculation
aanzfta_duty.notes: AANZFTA provides preferential rates for Australian and New Zealand goods. Most tariffs reduced to 0% or minimal rates.

dq_adjustment.description: DQ (Deal/Trade Agreement) - Real deal or trade agreement between one company and the government, specific to Cambodia Customs
dq_adjustment.notes: DQ is a user-provided adjustment factor. No backend registry — the user must supply dq_factor directly when dq_applicable is true.

sop_amount.description: SOP Amount - Calculated result, optionally adjusted by company-specific DQ when applicable, ALWAYS rounded UP to nearest 100
sop_amount.notes: SOP includes all standard calculations. When DQ applies, the company-specific dq_factor adjusts the SOP amount before rounding. Final amount ALWAYS rounds UP to nearest 100, never down.

cop_amount.description: COP Amount - Calculated WITH Customs Duty Rate applied, ALWAYS rounded UP to nearest 100
cop_amount.notes: COP is the amount calculated with the official customs duty rate. Final amount ALWAYS rounds UP to nearest 100, never down.

commodity_tax_by_mass.description: Calculate tax based on net mass in kilograms (used for commodities like rubber)
commodity_tax_by_mass.notes: Some commodities are taxed based on weight rather than value. Net mass must be accurately declared.

commodity_tax_by_volume.description: Calculate tax based on volume in liters (used for commodities like petroleum)
commodity_tax_by_volume.notes: Petroleum and similar products are typically taxed per liter. Volume must be temperature-corrected to standard conditions.

commodity_tax_hybrid.description: Calculate tax using both net mass and volume (for certain rubber and petroleum cases)
commodity_tax_hybrid.notes: Most frequently used case for rubber and petroleum where both mass and volume determine the tax liability.

final_amount_with_rounding.description: Apply rounding ONLY when money is ready to pay - ALWAYS round UP to nearest 100, never down
final_amount_with_rounding.notes: CRITICAL: Apply this ONLY to final payment amounts when ready to pay. Do NOT apply to tax base amounts (CIF, duty, excise, VAT, total_duties_and_taxes).

normal_case_customs_value.description: NORMAL CASE: Calculate customs value from item price and exchange rate
normal_case_customs_value.notes: Standard customs valuation for regular imports

normal_case_cop.description: NORMAL CASE: COP (Customs of Payment) = customs value × rate
normal_case_cop.notes: COP is the customs duty amount in normal import scenarios

normal_case_sop.description: NORMAL CASE: SOP (Special tax/Excise) = (customs value + COP amount) × rate
normal_case_sop.notes: SOP is calculated on the base of customs value plus COP

vop_non_taxable_goods.description: VOP for NON-TAXABLE GOODS: VOP = (Customs Value + COP) × 10%
vop_non_taxable_goods.condition: When SOP rate is 0% or good is exempted from special tax
vop_non_taxable_goods.notes: Non-taxable goods: SOP = 0%, so VOP includes only CIF + COP

vop_taxable_goods.description: VOP for TAXABLE GOODS: VOP = (Customs Value + COP + SOP) × 10%
vop_taxable_goods.condition: When SOP rate > 0% (good has special tax/excise)
vop_taxable_goods.notes: Taxable goods: SOP applies, so VOP includes CIF + COP + SOP

normal_case_vop.description: NORMAL CASE: VOP (VAT on Payment) - CONDITIONAL based on good type
normal_case_vop.notes: CRITICAL: Check SOP rate first. If SOP = 0%, exclude SOP from VOP base. If SOP > 0%, include SOP in VOP base.

petroleum_phase1_cpp_base.description: PETROLEUM PHASE 1: CPP base = (DV × Exchange Rate × Net Mass) / 1000
petroleum_phase1_cpp_base.notes: CPP base for petroleum using Declared Value and net mass in kg

petroleum_phase1_cpp.description: PETROLEUM PHASE 1: CPP (Customs Petroleum Payment) = CPP base × Rate
petroleum_phase1_cpp.notes: Customs duty for petroleum in phase 1

petroleum_phase1_atp.description: PETROLEUM PHASE 1: ATP (Additional Tax Petroleum) = LTR × Rate × Exchange Rate
petroleum_phase1_atp.notes: ATP base = LTR (Liter volume). Additional tax based on volume

petroleum_phase1_spp.description: PETROLEUM PHASE 1: SPP (Special tax Petroleum) = (CPP base + CPP + ATP) × Rate

petroleum_phase1_vpp_base.description: PETROLEUM PHASE 1: VPP base = SPP base + SPP Amount
petroleum_phase1_vpp_base.notes: Base for VAT calculation in petroleum phase 1. SPP base = CPP base + CPP + ATP

petroleum_phase1_vpp.description: PETROLEUM PHASE 1: VPP (VAT Petroleum) = VPP base × Rate

petroleum_phase2.description: PETROLEUM PHASE 2: Same as Phase 1 but replace CPP base with actual CUSTOMS VALUE
petroleum_phase2.notes: Phase 2 uses actual customs value instead of calculated CPP base

petroleum_dpp.description: PETROLEUM: DPP (Partial subsidy by the state) = Phase 1 - Phase 2
petroleum_dpp.notes: DPP represents the partial subsidy by the state, calculated from the difference between two-phase petroleum calculations

rubber_etr.description: RUBBER CASE: ETR (Export Tax on Rubber) = (DV × Exchange Rate × Net Mass) / 1000
rubber_etr.notes: Export tax on rubber based on Declared Value and net mass in kg

fta_dv_case_cop.description: FTA/DV CASE: COP = Customs Value × Rate = 0 (typically)
fta_dv_case_cop.notes: For FTA (Free Trade Agreement) with DV, COP is typically 0%

fta_dv_case_cop_amount.description: FTA/DV CASE: COP Amount = Customs Value × Customs Duty Rate
fta_dv_case_cop_amount.notes: Even when duty is 0%, this shows the calculated customs duty amount

fta_dv_case_sop.description: FTA/DV CASE: SOP = (Custom Value + COP Amount) × Rate
fta_dv_case_sop.notes: SOP calculated even when COP is 0 under FTA

fta_dv_case_vop_non_taxable.condition: When good under FTA has 0% special tax
fta_dv_case_vop_non_taxable.notes: FTA non-taxable goods: COP typically 0%, SOP = 0%, VOP on (CIF + COP)

fta_dv_case_vop_taxable.condition: When good under FTA still has special tax (e.g., smartphones with ATIGA)
fta_dv_case_vop_taxable.notes: FTA taxable goods: COP typically 0% but SOP applies, VOP on (CIF + COP + SOP)

fta_dv_case_vop.description: FTA/DV CASE: VOP - CONDITIONAL based on good type

if_sop_is_zero.example: Most FTA goods with 0% duty and 0% special tax

if_sop_greater_than_zero.example: Smartphones with ATIGA Form D still have 5% ST

fta_dv_case_vop.notes: Even under FTA (0% COP), VAT still applies. Check SOP to determine if it's included in VOP base.

fta_dv_dq_case_cop.description: FTA/DV & DQ CASE: COP = COP base × Rate = 0
fta_dv_dq_case_cop.notes: COP is 0 under FTA even with DQ adjustment

fta_dv_dq_case_sop_base.description: FTA/DV & DQ CASE: SOP base = Customs Value + COP Amount
fta_dv_dq_case_sop_base.notes: Base calculation for SOP before DQ adjustment

fta_dv_dq_case_sop.description: FTA/DV & DQ CASE: SOP = (SOP base + COP base) × Rate × DQ
fta_dv_dq_case_sop.notes: SOP with DQ (Deal/Trade Agreement) adjustment applied

fta_dv_dq_case_vop_base.formula: CONDITIONAL: (CIF + COP) OR (CIF + COP + DQ-adjusted SOP)
fta_dv_dq_case_vop_base.description: FTA/DV & DQ CASE: VOP base - CONDITIONAL based on good type
fta_dv_dq_case_vop_base.notes: Check SOP rate first. DQ adjustment only applies to SOP when SOP > 0%

fta_dv_dq_case_vop_non_taxable.notes: FTA/DQ non-taxable: VOP on (CIF + COP), DQ adjustment not needed

fta_dv_dq_case_vop_taxable.description: FTA/DV & DQ CASE (Taxable): VOP = (CIF + COP + DQ-adjusted SOP) × 10%
fta_dv_dq_case_vop_taxable.condition: When good has special tax (and DQ-adjusted SOP is included)
fta_dv_dq_case_vop_taxable.notes: FTA/DQ taxable: VOP on (CIF + COP + DQ-adjusted SOP). Use SOP amount after DQ adjustment.

fta_dv_dq_case_vop.formula: CONDITIONAL: (CIF + COP) × 10% OR (CIF + COP + DQ-adjusted SOP) × 10%
fta_dv_dq_case_vop.description: FTA/DV & DQ CASE: VOP - CONDITIONAL based on good type
fta_dv_dq_case_vop.notes: DQ adjustment affects SOP calculation. Include DQ-adjusted SOP in VOP base when SOP > 0%.

normal_case.description: Standard import calculation for regular goods
normal_case.when_to_use: Default case for most imports without special conditions
sequence: 0. Currency Conversion: If USD, convert to KHR using MEF exchange rate
1. Customs Value = Exchange Rate × Item Price
2. COP = Customs Value × COP Rate
3. SOP = (Customs Value + COP) × SOP Rate
4a. IF SOP = 0% (Non-taxable goods): VOP = (CIF + COP) × 10%
4b. IF SOP > 0% (Taxable goods): VOP = (CIF + COP + SOP) × 10%
5. Apply final rounding (round UP to 100)

example.scenario: Company A imports 20 cases of beer with Customs Value of 4,000,000 KHR

normal_case.important_note: CRITICAL: Check SOP rate BEFORE calculating VOP. Non-taxable goods (SOP=0%) use simpler VOP formula. Taxable goods (SOP>0%) include SOP in VOP base.

petroleum_case.when_to_use: When importing petroleum products that require volume and mass-based calculations
phase_1: 0. Currency Conversion: If USD, convert to KHR using MEF exchange rate
1. CPP base = (DV × Exchange Rate × Net Mass) / 1000
3. ATP = LTR × ATP Rate × Exchange Rate
4. SPP = (CPP base + CPP + ATP) × SPP Rate
phase_2: Same as Phase 1 but replace CPP base with actual CUSTOMS VALUE
petroleum_case.note: Petroleum requires both mass (Net Mass in kg) and volume (LTR) measurements. DV is now an external input when provided; otherwise it is derived from customs value for backward compatibility.

rubber_case.description: Export tax calculation for rubber based on mass
sequence: 0. Currency Conversion: If USD, convert to KHR using MEF exchange rate
1. ETR = (DV × Exchange Rate × Net Mass) / 1000
rubber_case.note: Net Mass must be in kilograms. DV is now an external input when provided; otherwise customs value is used for backward compatibility.

fta_dv_case.description: Free Trade Agreement with Declared Value (duty typically 0%)
fta_dv_case.when_to_use: When goods qualify for FTA preferential treatment with DV valuation
sequence: 0. Currency Conversion: If USD, convert to KHR using MEF exchange rate
1. COP = Customs Value × Rate = 0 (typically, FTA rate)
2. COP Amount = Customs Value × Customs Duty Rate (shows 0 amount)
3. SOP = (Customs Value + COP Amount) × SOP Rate
4a. IF SOP = 0% (Non-taxable FTA goods): VOP = (CIF + COP) × 10%
4b. IF SOP > 0% (Taxable FTA goods): VOP = (CIF + COP + SOP) × 10%
5. Apply final rounding (round UP to 100)
fta_dv_case.note: Even though COP is 0% under FTA, SOP and VAT are still calculated. DV can be provided as the customs valuation basis; otherwise customs value is used. Check SOP to determine VOP base. Example: Smartphones with ATIGA Form D have 0% CD but 5% ST.

fta_dv_dq_case.description: FTA with DV and DQ Deal/Trade Agreement adjustment
fta_dv_dq_case.when_to_use: When goods qualify for FTA and there is a DQ agreement between one company and the government
sequence: 0. Currency Conversion: If USD, convert to KHR using MEF exchange rate
1. COP = COP base × Rate = 0 (FTA rate)
2. COP Amount = Customs Value × Customs Duty Rate (shows 0 amount)
3. SOP base = Customs Value + COP Amount
4. SOP = (SOP base + COP base) × SOP Rate × DQ (with DQ adjustment)
5a. IF SOP = 0% (Non-taxable): VOP = (CIF + COP) × 10%
5b. IF SOP > 0% (Taxable): VOP = (CV + COP + DQ-adjusted SOP) × 10%
6. Apply final rounding (round UP to 100)
fta_dv_dq_case.note: DQ factor is now an external input for future changes. It adjusts the SOP calculation. Use DQ-adjusted SOP in VOP base for taxable goods.

acronym_definitions.COP: Import Taxes - Customs value multiplied by import tax rate
acronym_definitions.SOP: Special Tariff - (Customs Value + Import Taxes) multiplied by special tariff rate
acronym_definitions.VOP: VAT of Payment - Value Added Tax amount
acronym_definitions.CPP: Customs Petroleum Payment - Customs duty for petroleum
acronym_definitions.ATP: Additional Tax Petroleum - Volume-based tax on petroleum
acronym_definitions.SPP: Special Petroleum Payment - Excise tax for petroleum
acronym_definitions.VPP: VAT Petroleum Payment - VAT for petroleum
acronym_definitions.DPP: Partial subsidy by the state for petroleum products
acronym_definitions.ETR: Export Tax on Rubber - Export tax for rubber based on mass
acronym_definitions.DV: Declared Value - Fair amount of price that keeps the market in the middle, not too high or too low
acronym_definitions.DQ: Deal/Trade Agreement - Cambodia Customs-specific agreement between one company and the government
acronym_definitions.FTA: Free Trade Agreement - Preferential trade agreement with 0% or reduced duty
acronym_definitions.ATIGA: ASEAN Trade in Goods Agreement - Intra-ASEAN FTA (Form D) - Most commonly used in Cambodia
acronym_definitions.RCEP: Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (Form RCEP) - Covers 15 countries
acronym_definitions.AANZFTA: ASEAN-Australia-New Zealand Free Trade Agreement (Form AANZ)

calculation_sequence: currency_conversion (if currency is USD, convert to KHR FIRST)
acfta_duty OR import_duty OR preferential_duty OR duty_exemption
excise_tax OR specific_tax OR commodity_tax_by_mass OR commodity_tax_by_volume OR commodity_tax_hybrid
total_duties_and_taxes (round to whole number, do NOT round to 100)
sop_amount (with company-specific DQ when applicable) - ROUND UP to 100
cop_amount (with customs duty rate) - ROUND UP to 100
final_amount_with_rounding (apply ONLY when money is ready to pay)

cambodia_specific_rules.dv: Declared Value is the fair amount of price used as the customs valuation basis to keep the market in the middle, not too high or too low
cambodia_specific_rules.acfta: ASEAN-China FTA makes duty rate 0% for eligible goods
cambodia_specific_rules.dq: DQ is a Cambodia Customs-specific real deal or trade agreement between one company and the government; it is not a formal customs term used in other countries. Each company can have a different DQ factor/agreement.
cambodia_specific_rules.sop_vs_cop: SOP/SPP/ETR can be adjusted by company-specific DQ when applicable; COP includes customs duty rate calculation
cambodia_specific_rules.commodity_units: Rubber and petroleum are most common cases requiring net mass (kg) and/or volume (LTR) based calculations
cambodia_specific_rules.rounding: All amounts round UP to nearest 100 (12345.04 → 12400, 12345.05 → 12400).
cambodia_specific_rules.export_note: These calculations apply to IMPORTS only; exports do not use DV

rounding_rules.note: All amounts (intermediate and final) round UP to nearest 100 (12345.04 → 12400, 12345.05 → 12400).

notes: All calculations use CIF value or DV (Declared Value) as the customs valuation basis
VAT is calculated on the aggregate of CIF + Duty + Excise
Preferential rates require valid Certificate of Origin
Exemptions require proper authorization and documentation
Currency conversion: Use fixed table method with official MEF exchange rates (see exchange_rate_policy.json for complete policy)
Special procedures (QIP, bonded warehouse, temporary admission) may have different calculation rules
CRITICAL: Round UP to 100 ONLY for final payment amounts (total_payable, sop_amount, cop_amount) - NOT for tax base amounts
All amounts (CIF, duty, excise, VAT, total_duties_and_taxes) round UP to nearest 100 (12345.04 → 12400, 12345.05 → 12400)
FTA AGREEMENTS - Cambodia participates in multiple FTAs. Most commonly used:
1. ATIGA (Form D) - Intra-ASEAN trade, 0% duty on most goods - MOST COMMONLY USED IN CAMBODIA
2. ACFTA (Form E) - ASEAN-China trade, 0% duty on eligible goods
3. RCEP (Form RCEP) - Regional agreement covering 15 countries, progressive tariff elimination
4. AKFTA (Form AK) - ASEAN-Korea trade, preferential rates (typically 0%)
5. AJCEP (Form AJ) - ASEAN-Japan trade, preferential rates (typically 0% or reduced)
6. AANZFTA (Form AANZ) - ASEAN-Australia-NZ trade, preferential rates
All FTAs require valid Certificate of Origin and commodity eligibility verification
Even with 0% customs duty under FTA, SOP (excise) and VOP (VAT) still apply to most goods
DQ (Deal/Trade Agreement) is Cambodia Customs-specific and represents a real deal or trade agreement between one company and the government; different companies can have different DQ factors
SOP/SPP/ETR Amount = calculation with company-specific DQ adjustment when applicable (rounded UP to 100 when ready to pay)
COP Amount = calculation with customs duty rate applied (rounded UP to 100 when ready to pay)
Rubber and petroleum commonly require calculations based on Net Mass (kg) and/or Volume (LTR)
Even if not counted in COP section, amounts must still be calculated for SOP
These rules apply to IMPORTS only; exports do not use DV or these specific calculations
Net mass and volume measurements must be accurate and verified during customs inspection
CALCULATION CASES: Use 'calculation_cases' section to determine which formulas to apply based on product type and trade conditions
NORMAL CASE: Standard imports use COP → SOP → VOP sequence
PETROLEUM CASE: Requires two-phase calculation with DPP = Phase1 - Phase2
RUBBER CASE: Uses ETR (Export Tax on Rubber) formula based on DV, exchange rate, and net mass
FTA/DV CASE: Free trade agreement with 0% duty but SOP and VOP still apply
FTA/DV & DQ CASE: FTA with Deal/Trade Agreement adjustment affecting SOP calculation
See 'acronym_definitions' for meaning of COP, SOP, VOP, CPP, ATP, SPP, VPP, DPP, ETR
See 'exchange_rate_policy.json' for currency conversion rules, rate selection, and data source specifications
See 'rounding_rules.json' for all rounding policies (quantities, rates, amounts, and conversions)
